corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science work on large language models, the corpus reveals emergent concerns and opportunities at the intersection of human–AI interaction, AI-enabled research methods, education, and governance. Studies map trust, perceived humanness, and social influence; demonstrate LLMs as toolchains for analysis, planning, and policy; document learning benefits and risks in classrooms and health contexts; and call for equitable, transparent oversight.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction and trust dynamics
themes.description: The records show how trust, perceived humanness, presentation formats, and social influences shape user preferences, adoption, and wellbeing across health, education, and everyday tasks.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological innovation
themes.description: A wide range of studies demonstrates LLMs enabling data extraction, coding, sentiment analysis, policy analysis, and simulation, while stressing validation, reproducibility, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: Education, learning, and AI literacy
themes.description: Evidence covers AI-assisted tutoring, classroom deployment, teacher readiness, and AI literacy interventions for diverse learners, highlighting benefits and risks like overreliance and equity concerns.

themes.name: Equity, bias, ethics, and governance of AI
themes.description: Papers evaluate fairness across identities, cultural adequacy, misinformation, and governance frameworks to ensure safe, inclusive AI deployment.
